findings.summary: Broad except Exception: pass silently drops ALL context macros if any single value in _macros lacks .func (Executable has no .func, and the type is ExecutableOrMacro)
findings.failure_scenario: If any entry in context.context._macros is an Executable (which lacks .func), getattr(m.func, '__doc__', None) raises AttributeError on m.func evaluation -- not on the getattr itself, so the default=None never comes into play. The except Exception: pass then discards every remaining context macro, not just the failing one. Type annotation explicitly allows ExecutableOrMacro values.

findings.summary: multiply docstring renders with an unmatched opening double-quote because the closing " of "column > 0" is consumed by the """ delimiter
findings.failure_scenario: The docstring literal is """untyped column will be a sqlglot column and return a sqlglot exp "column > 0""". Python's tokenizer treats the final three " as the closing """, so the docstring content becomes: 'untyped column will be a sqlglot column and return a sqlglot exp "column > 0' -- with a stray unmatched " that was meant to be the opening quote of "column > 0". Cosmetic documentation defect; no runtime crash.
